title: OTPCL: Optimal Transport Driven Pseudo-Labeling with Contrastive Learning for Social Bot Detection

problem.claim: Social bot detection must identify coordinated bot behaviors in social networks where heterophilous interactions can disrupt GNN message passing and labeled data are sparse.

gap.claim: Existing GNN-based approaches are challenged by cross-class ties and underutilize the large amount of unlabeled social-media data.

contributions.claim: OTPCL is a plug-in framework for GNN-based social bot detection that combines contrastive learning, optimal-transport pseudo-labeling, and transport-score-guided graph and label refinement.
The framework uses optimal transport to generate pseudo-labels and quantify their reliability, then removes unreliable heterophilous edges and downweights pseudo-labels below a dynamic threshold.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three benchmark datasets reportedly show consistent detection-performance improvements across six GNN backbones.
The authors report robustness and generalization in both low-labeled and fully-labeled scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Social bot detection is important for protecting online platforms from misinformation and manipulation.
GNNs use relational patterns and social interactions to detect coordinated bot behaviors.
Heterophilous edges undermine homophily-based message passing, while sparse labels leave unlabeled data underutilized.
OTPCL combines contrastive representations, optimal-transport pseudo-labeling, reliability scoring, edge removal, and pseudo-label weighting.
The authors report improvements across multiple GNN backbones and labeling settings on three benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: Cross-class interactions can cause graph message passing to propagate errors when models rely on homophily.

interpretation.claim: Graph-learning systems may benefit from identifying and reducing the influence of structurally unreliable edges.

application.claim: Use reliability-guided graph refinement when applying GNNs to networks with substantial cross-class interaction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether edge removal helps outside social bot detection or under different graph structures.

source_observation.claim: Transport scores are used to quantify pseudo-label reliability and control pseudo-label influence.

interpretation.claim: Confidence-aware use of unlabeled data can make sparse supervision more effective.

application.claim: In semi-supervised graph learning, use confidence estimates to select or weight pseudo-labels rather than treating them uniformly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the reliability calibration, thresholding procedure, or error behavior of the pseudo-labels.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets or report quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, ablations, or failure cases.
